messages.content: Show me a textbook-quality diagram illustrating length comparison towers

Here's a textbook-quality diagram illustrating length comparison towers for kindergarten math:

%%TIKZ_GRAPH%%{"description":"Draw three vertical towers of colored blocks on a horizontal base. Left tower: 3 red blocks (each 1 unit tall). Middle tower: 2 blue blocks (each 1.5 units tall). Right tower: 1 green block (3 units tall). Add labels '3 red blocks', '2 blue blocks', and '1 green block' below each tower respectively. Add a horizontal line at the top of each tower to show the same height. Add a caption 'Which tower is the tallest?'","engine":"pure_tikz","course_hint":"kindergarten_math","archetype_hint":"comparison_towers","extra_rules":""}%%END_TIKZ_GRAPH%%

This diagram shows three towers made of different colored blocks. Each tower has a different number of blocks, but all blocks in a single tower are the same size. The horizontal line at the top shows that all towers are the same height, even though they have different numbers of blocks. This helps children understand that objects can have the same length even if they're made up of different numbers of smaller pieces.

This activity aligns with kindergarten math standards related to measurement and geometry (K.MG.1, K.MG.2), as it helps students compare lengths and understand that length can be measured using different units.
